note: Adapted from the species description of Sands (1972); the original is in English and the genus has no soldier caste, only the alate and worker being described; measurement tables, figure numbers, type specimens and distribution records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The largest species of the genus, although A. murcus, the largest specimens of A. brevior and A. empodius approach it in size. The characters separating it from A. murcus have been given above; the remaining comparisons are given in the discussion of A. ignavus and A. mitis. In A. brevior the mandibular proportions differ in both castes and the enteric valve seating is sessile. The proportions of the mandibular teeth also separate A. empodius, which in addition has a markedly lobed, sessile enteric valve seating. The species was originally placed in Alyscotermes, but the enteric valve of that genus has conspicuous spiny structures and the third apical spur of the fore tibia of the worker is well developed rather than reduced. The abdomen of the worker appears able to dehisce, though not very obviously; the specimens did not disintegrate completely.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule orange yellow, pilosity yellowish brown, sparse and long, coarse and conspicuous. Postclypeus weakly inflated, Pcl/W 0.25, Pcl/Ri 2.39; apical tooth of mandibles moderately long, La/Li 0.73, Ra/Ri 1.00; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible separated from the molar prominence in surface view by a wide notch, compound ratio 9.30; first marginal tooth of the right mandible very slightly posterior to the line from the apical to the second marginal tooth, the anterior edge of the first marginal tooth slightly longer than that of the second, compound ratio 13.09. Fore tibia slender, Ti/Ty 5.96, third apical spur reduced, not more than one fifth the length of the other two. Junction of mesenteron and proctodaeum slightly longer than oblique, to the right of the Malpighian nodule; enteric valve seating dorsal in the undissected abdomen, very weakly bilobed, connected to the second proctodaeal pouch by a long neck; membranous wall of the valve with sparse spinules outside the inner cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark chestnut brown, very deep above the ocelli; fontanelle oval, slightly smaller than the ocellus, slightly depressed, chestnut brown; mid-spot oval, flat, as large as or slightly smaller than the fontanelle, concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal mark distinct, a depressed chestnut brown crescent; antennae brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotum chestnut brown, transverse dark suture present; femora yellowish brown, tibiae paler, tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites, dorsal and ventral spiracles and the sides of the sternites brown; middle of the sternites and cerci pale yellowish brown. Posterior margin of head capsule evenly rounded; ocelli rather small, separated from the compound eye by two-thirds to five-sixths of their own minimum diameter; postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.26–0.27, Pcl/Ra 2.92–3.17, posterior margin evenly rounded, median suture distinct. Apical tooth of mandibles short, La/Li 0.52, Ra/Ri 0.76–0.78; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible separated from the molar prominence in surface view by a wide notch, compound ratio 5.21–5.22; apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible in the same line, the anterior edge of the first marginal tooth nearly twice as long as that of the second. Pilosity of head capsule chestnut brown, uneven, not felted. Constriction between meso- and metanotum distinctly wide, M/W 0.33–0.36. Third apical spur of fore tibia only slightly smaller than the other two.
